text.brief: Deng Xiaoping put on a ten-gallon hat at a rodeo outside Houston on February 2, 1979.
text.record: The photograph ran on front pages across the country during a visit that began with the signing of the Agreement on Cooperation in Science and Technology on January 31 ([State Department treaty record: China (24-227), Agreement on Cooperation in Science and Technology (signed January 31, 1979)](https://www.state.gov/china-24-227); [State Department Office of the Historian: China, People's Republic of: Visits by Foreign Leaders](https://history.state.gov/departmenthistory/visits/china)). The agreement framed four decades of joint research under dozens of agency protocols. It reached its renewal date in August 2023 ([State Department treaty record: China (24-227), extension of the Science and Technology Agreement (exchange of notes February 22 and 27, 2024)](https://www.state.gov/china-24-227)). After short extensions the State Department renewed it in December 2024 with a narrower scope that leaves out critical and emerging technologies ([State Department: Amendment and Extension of the U.S.-PRC Science and Technology Agreement (December 13, 2024)](https://2021-2025.state.gov/amendment-and-extension-of-the-u-s-prc-science-and-technology-agreement-sta/); [State Department treaty record: China (24-1213), protocol amending and extending the agreement](https://www.state.gov/china-24-1213)).
text.reading: The hat bought goodwill on the evening news, while the agreement bought access to American laboratories for forty years, which is Stratagem 17. Americans enjoyed the gesture and seldom counted what the framework carried.
text.gapText: Business Architecture. No agency owned the total cost of the agreement, so each protocol answered only to its own sponsor.
text.fix: Renew science agreements on fixed terms with a published list of closed fields, and review every protocol against it.
